Sodomie.et: From Late Latin sodomia, from the Biblical town Sodom (Genesis 18f.), from Ancient Greek Σόδομα (Sódoma), from Hebrew סדם (səḏōm).

Sodbrennen.et: From Middle High German sote (“boil”) + brennen (“to burn”).

s: Er hat sich verletzt, sodass er beim Spiel nicht eingesetzt werden konnte.

Soda.et: Borrowed from Spanish soda. Beverage uses are from semantic loan from English soda.

s: one who engages in anal sex, especially homosexual, and especially the active partner
Sodomist.et: From Sodomie + -ist. Alternatively analysable as Sodom + -ist.

s: sodomite (person who has sex with animals)

sodann.et: From Middle High German sōdanne, from Old High German sōdanne. By surface analysis, univerbation of so + dann.

s: Used to express completion, or reinforcement of an action or statement; there, alright
Sodala, das macht dann 9,99 Euro, bitte.
sodala.et: so (“so”) + da (“there”) with an added rhyming syllable.
